article_title: Supplemental Material for Important Text Characteristics for Early-Grades Text Complexity
citation: J. Fitzgerald et al. (2014). Important Text Characteristics for Early-Grades Text Complexity. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0037289
title: Corpus of 350 early-grades texts used for complexity measurement and prediction
description: The study's material base is a set of 350 early-grades texts, stratified by six categories and publisher-designated difficulty level for sampling. The 350 texts were digitized (including images) for teacher comparison, all 350 were assigned teacher-judgment logit scores and 0–100 complexity measures, and a random stratified sample of 90 texts (89 analyzed) was read by students. Text characteristics were computer- operationalized for these texts as predictors on the text-complexity outcome measure.
requirements: Texts must be digitizable, including images, for side-by-side computer-screen comparison by teachers
constraints: Student maze testing sampled only a subset of 90 texts from the 350, so student-based logits exist for fewer texts than teacher-based logits
target_learning_goals: Measuring and predicting early-reader text-complexity level
examples: A random sample of 90 texts was selected stratified by the six categories and by publisher-designated difficulty level; one passage was later rejected due to a printing error
key_sources: J. Fitzgerald et al. (2014). Important Text Characteristics for Early-Grades Text Complexity. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0037289

article_title: Evaluation of primary care physicians' knowledge, attitudes, and awareness levels regarding age-related macular degeneration.
citation: Öncül Hasan, Dertsiz Kozan Betül, Dağ Umut, Çağlayan Mehtap, Alakuş Mehmet Fuat, Temel Cengiz, Utlu Elif Sedanur. (2026). Evaluation of primary care physicians’ knowledge, attitudes, and awareness levels regarding age-related macular degeneration. BMC Primary Care. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12875-026-03228-2
title: 35-item AMD knowledge, attitude, and awareness questionnaire for primary care physicians
description: A self-administered online questionnaire developed by the researchers, consisting of demographic items and "35 closed-ended questions assessing the participants’ knowledge, attitudes, and clinical approaches regarding AMD." Each correct knowledge response scored 1 point (total 0–35), with tertile bands: low 0–11, basic 12–22, good 23–35. Content validity was evaluated by a three-ophthalmologist panel (CVI 0.82), piloted with 20 family physicians, with knowledge-domain Cronbach's alpha of 0.78.
requirements: Administered online with items scored 1 point for correct responses and 0 for incorrect or “I have no idea” responses
constraints: The authors state the instrument "did not evaluate key clinical decision-making skills such as diagnosis, differential diagnosis, referral decisions, recognition of early clinical symptoms" and should be interpreted as reflecting general awareness rather than comprehensive clinical competence
target_learning_goals: Assessment of AMD knowledge, attitudes, and clinical approaches
examples: Used in the August–September 2025 cross-sectional survey of 440 primary care physicians in Türkiye; three items (Q6, Q9, Q11) were administered as multiple-choice questions on age of onset, legal blindness rate, and dry-type proportion.
key_sources: Öncül Hasan, Dertsiz Kozan Betül, Dağ Umut, Çağlayan Mehtap, Alakuş Mehmet Fuat, Temel Cengiz, Utlu Elif Sedanur. (2026). Evaluation of primary care physicians’ knowledge, attitudes, and awareness levels regarding age-related macular degeneration. BMC Primary Care. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12875-026-03228-2
